thesis: Precise distinctions prevent moral standing, agency and forms of duty from collapsing into blame.

ideas.statement: Moral considerability is distinct from agency, and prospective duties need no prior blame.
An excuse reduces blame while a justification defends the act; limits of special duty and supererogation remain disputed.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Definitions describe contested families of positions rather than settling every dispute.

audit.notes: All assigned units read. Claims remain bounded; hypothetical cases are not empirical evidence.
